calls.head: Airtight vs. leaky on the kill
calls.body: On the penalty kill, Anaheim is near the top of the league, but San Jose is one of the worst. Penalties are likely to hurt the Sharks more than the Ducks. Anaheim’s penalty kill has been near the bottom of the league for years, though. These two hand each other plenty of power plays, so special teams should get a real say.

surprises.head: Anaheim kept finding open men against Alex Nedeljkovic
surprises.body: Nedeljkovic allowed 7 goals on 30 shots, worth 2.3 expected goals: 4.7 more than expected, though five of them came off a pass that set up the shooter. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 500 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

story.head: Brossoit slams the door on the Sharks
paras: An ugly night for the Sharks. Judd Caulfield and Alex Killorn scored 30 seconds apart midway through the first to put the Ducks up 2-0. Cutter Gauthier extended the lead to 3-0 on the power play just over a minute later, and Ian Moore made it 4-0 midway through the second. Roger McQueen stretched the lead to 5-0 just under two minutes later, with Nico Myatovic picking up his first NHL point on the goal. Frank Vatrano and Killorn scored less than four minutes apart midway through the third to make it 7-0, and the Sharks had no answer. Mikael Granlund finished with three assists.

Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Laurent Brossoit stopped all 23 shots for the Ducks, and Alex Nedeljkovic allowed seven goals on 30 shots. The Ducks moved to 12-13-1 and took third place in the Pacific from the Sharks, who dropped to 11-14-2.

items.text: The Ducks won for the first time in five games.
All four of the preview’s calls held.
